note: Daily orders at 1.1× the forecast for the arrival day, a bit above the multiplier's mean of 1.046, with no orders that would arrive after day 29; the main risk is shortages on high-demand days.
Exactly the forecast, every day; risk: systematic under-ordering, since the multiplier's mean is 1.046, plus noise means frequent penalties.
1.2× buffer stock; risk: the surplus builds up and gets written off at expiry, with purchase costs wasted.

Batching both items every other day on the same days (~1.1× two days' demand) saves about 13×51 in fixed fees; risk: overflowing the 284-unit warehouse around days 18–20 (item 1 gets lost) and higher holding costs.
A middle ground at 1.05×, matching the multiplier's mean; risk: more shortage penalties than at 1.1.

Asymmetric: item 0, which keeps 7 days, gets a bigger 1.15× buffer, while item 1, which keeps 4 days, gets 1.05×; the final item 0 orders are tapered because stock left at the end is worthless. Risk: item 1 shortages.
Aggressive 1.3× to get rid of shortages; risk: large write-offs and capacity overflow at the demand peaks.
Lean 0.9× with minimal write-offs; risk: lost margin and constant penalties, since margin plus penalty (13–14 per unit) far exceeds the cost of a surplus unit.
